sections.overview: Eudendrium dispar is a valid hydroid species in the cnidarian class Hydrozoa, reported from the western Atlantic.
sections.identification: The species belongs to Eudendriidae; genus-level colonies are upright and irregularly branched, but shape alone is not diagnostic.
sections.habitat: The species is recorded in the western Atlantic; genus-level accounts describe hydroids attached to hard surfaces, often in shaded places.
sections.diet: As a hydroid, it has feeding polyps, but the consulted sources do not establish prey or diet specifically for this species.
sections.behavior: It is a fixed colonial animal rather than a free-swimming adult; the available species pages offer little behavioral detail.
sections.reproduction: Reproductive structures are important in distinguishing Eudendrium species, but a species-specific seasonal cycle was not verified here.
sections.ecology: The genus grows on hard natural or biological surfaces, including rock, pebbles and shells; these are genus-level observations.
sections.conservation: The reviewed taxonomic records provide no species-level conservation assessment or population trend for Eudendrium dispar.
